faq: Why did my printer stop working?

The printer maker's Mac driver was built for older Intel Macs and never updated. macOS 27 marks those drivers as incompatible, so the printer stops, even though nothing is wrong with it. This free driver replaces the old one.
Will reinstalling Rosetta fix it?

Sometimes, and only for now. Reinstalling Rosetta makes some old printer drivers work again after you delete and re-add the printer; others stay marked “Software Incompatible”. Apple ends Rosetta for apps in macOS 28, so the maker's old driver will stop again then. This driver doesn't need Rosetta.
I had the printer maker's old driver installed. Anything to do?
Restart the Mac once after installing, then unplug and re-plug the printer. The installer moves Canon's old driver aside, nothing is deleted.
Still on macOS 26 Tahoe or earlier?
Your printer works now, but it can stop after you update. You can install this before or after updating.
My printer is on Wi-Fi, not USB.
Install the driver, then open System Settings → Printers & Scanners, click Add, select your printer, choose Use: Select Software… and pick your model ending in “Apple Silicon”.
The installer didn't add my printer.
Install the driver, then open System Settings → Printers & Scanners, click Add, select your printer, choose Use: Select Software… and pick your model ending in “Apple Silicon”.
Where are print quality and black & white?
In the print dialog, open Printer Features (Printer Options on macOS 27). Quality is under Resolution. For black & white set Color Model to Grayscale.
Black doesn't print, or colors look off.

Run a nozzle check from the printer itself first: an empty or clogged cartridge is the usual cause. Then check in Printer Features that no “color-only” mode is selected. Colors can look a little different from the maker's driver.
Supply Levels says “Information Not Available”.
That's expected: this driver can't read ink or toner levels. Check them on the printer's own screen.
My printer isn't in the list.

Many newer printers support AirPrint and need no driver: connect the printer to your network, then add it in System Settings → Printers & Scanners → Add, with Use: AirPrint. AirPrint doesn't work over USB.
My Brother ink tank printer (DCP-T420W, DCP-T426W, DCP-T536DW, MFC-T…) isn't supported.

These printers have no free driver, so this package can't add them. Check your model's Downloads page on support.brother.com. If the printer supports AirPrint, connect it to your network and add it with Use: AirPrint.
My HP LaserJet 1018, 1020, P1005 or P1006 isn't supported.
These printers need HP's own software loaded every time they switch on, which this driver can't do. Picking a similar model doesn't work either: the job goes through, but nothing prints.
Does the scanner on my all-in-one work?
No, only printing. For scanning use VueScan (paid) or SANE (free, more technical).
Can I print from my iPhone or iPad?
Yes. Open Print from iPhone & iPad on your Mac and turn your printer on. Your Mac adds AirPrint for it, even over USB, as long as the Mac stays on.
Is it safe? Will macOS complain?
Yes, it's safe. The installer is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens without warnings, and everything it does is listed openly on GitHub.
Is it free?
Yes. Free and open source, no account needed. The driver collects nothing.
Which macOS versions?
Tested on macOS 27 on Apple Silicon. It should work on macOS 12 and later on Apple Silicon Macs.

help_h1: Printer still not working after installing?
help_lead: Fixes for the problems people hit after installing the driver package, in the order they usually happen.
trouble: It still says “The printer software is not compatible with this device” after installing.

That message belongs to the old printer entry, which still uses the maker's Intel-only driver. The installer adds a new entry next to it, named after the model and ending in “Apple Silicon”. In System Settings → Printers & Scanners, remove the old entry (select it, click −), then print to the “Apple Silicon” one. If there is no such entry, restart the Mac once, unplug and re-plug the printer, and check the next question.
My printer doesn't show up in the list.

Search your model on the home page first: if it isn't supported, no entry will appear. If it is supported and connected over USB, restart the Mac once and unplug / re-plug the printer, and connect it directly rather than through a hub or dock. Then add it in System Settings → Printers & Scanners → Add, with Use: Select Software… and the entry for your model ending in “Apple Silicon”.
“Software for this printer isn't available from Apple”.

macOS shows this when you add a printer it has no driver for. Install this package first, then add the printer again in System Settings → Printers & Scanners → Add, choose Use: Select Software… and pick the entry for your model ending in “Apple Silicon”.
“No AirPrint printers found”, or AirPrint isn't offered.

Older printers don't support AirPrint. On your Mac, add them with Use: Select Software… and the “Apple Silicon” entry, after installing this package. To print from an iPhone or iPad, turn the printer on in Print from iPhone & iPad, which adds AirPrint through your Mac, even over USB.
My printer is on Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

The installer only sets up USB printers by itself. For a network printer, add it in System Settings → Printers & Scanners → Add with Use: Select Software… and the “Apple Silicon” entry. If the printer doesn't appear, connect it to the same network as the Mac and switch it off and on.

Sometimes, and only for now. Reinstalling Rosetta makes some old printer drivers work again after you delete and re-add the printer; others stay marked “Software Incompatible”. Apple ends Rosetta for apps in macOS 28, so the maker's old driver will stop again then. This driver doesn't need Rosetta.
The job goes through but nothing prints, or only blank pages.

Check that the queue uses your exact model: a similar model's driver can send data the printer silently ignores. Some printers, such as the HP LaserJet 1018, 1020, P1005 and P1006, can't be supported at all because they need the maker's firmware sent on every power-up.

Open an issue on GitHub (https://github.com/theshiver/apple-silicon-printer-drivers/issues) with your printer model, how it's connected (USB or network) and your macOS version. Terminal steps for advanced users are in the README on GitHub.

iphone_need: The printer has to be set up on your Mac, and the Mac has to stay on and awake, on the same Wi-Fi as your iPhone.
iphone_faq: AirPrint is Apple's way to print from an iPhone or iPad with no app or driver on the phone. Older printers don't have it. This driver lets your Mac add it for them.
Can I print from my iPhone to a printer without AirPrint?
Yes. Set the printer up on your Mac, turn it on in Print from iPhone & iPad, and it shows up in the Print menu on your iPhone.
Does it work with HP, Canon, Brother and Epson printers?
Yes, with any printer set up on your Mac, including USB printers. Printers that already have AirPrint don't need this.
Does my Mac have to stay on?
Yes. Your iPhone prints through your Mac, so the Mac has to be on and awake, on the same Wi-Fi.
Can other people print to it?
Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can. It's off until you turn it on, and you pick which printers to share.
